runners_data.name: Havanagreattime
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse for Ruth Carr who has won twice on similar AW Standard going and was placed most recently over 6f here 19 days ago; stepping back up to 7f suits, and settling last before delivering late is exactly the profile this race shape rewards.
runners_data.comment: Havanagreattime arrives on the back of experience over today's trip and going, and his second five starts back shows he can threaten at this level; at 133 lb from stall three, though, the weight burden is the key question mark for a gelding yet to score in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Inside Story
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa takes the ride for James Tate and this three-year-old has a solid record at 7f on Standard surfaces, placing five times in eight starts; a prominent racer who will be embroiled in the early positional battle, and how he handles that scrimmage is the key variable.
runners_data.comment: Inside Story finished second last time out and her rating of 88 marks her as a genuine danger, with experience over today's trip and going working in her favour; the concern is that she remains yet to win in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Padua
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Hughie Morrison who has a modest record on Standard going (0W1P from 5 runs) and has not won over 7f on AW; Hector Crouch takes the ride and the horse carries a hood, but the 22-day absence and below-average sim-going figures temper expectations.
runners_data.comment: Padua won five starts back and shaped with promise when fourth two starts back, but a ninth last time out is hard to overlook; he has distance and going experience, and 132 lb from stall one gives the handicapper's view in numbers.

runners_data.name: Percy's Lad
runners_data.note: In cracking recent form — winning last time out 6 days ago at 7f Standard — and Daniel & Claire Kubler have a productive 5/16 trainer 14-day record; a prominent racer at OR 86 who is well-handicapped if he can avoid the early positional traffic, though eight-year-olds sometimes struggle when the fractions quicken sharply.
runners_data.comment: Percy's Lad arrives in good heart, winning last time out and second three starts back, and he has experience of both today's trip and going conditions; a slight query at 145 lb, but his profile makes him the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Naepoint
runners_data.note: Returning from 332 days off, which is a significant flag regardless of ability; the Richard & Peter Fahey yard has a solid strike rate (5/29 T14) but this horse won over 8f on softer ground and the step back to 7f on AW Standard represents an unknown quantity after such a lengthy absence.
runners_data.comment: Naepoint showed he knows how to win with a victory four starts back, and he has experience over today's trip and conditions, while his 87 rating underlines his claims; the concern is a lengthy 332-day absence that leaves fitness the key unknown.

runners_data.name: Haaderr
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's three-year-old is placed once and unbeaten at 7f on Standard going and arrives with a topspeed-friendly form profile; Daniel Tudhope rides and this prominent racer has the profile to handle the pace battle, though its sim-going record is a thin sample of just one qualifying run.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out keeps Haaderr in the mix, and a winner three starts back shows the ability is there; a trainer firing at 41% is a notable plus, though he carries 134 lb from stall 10 and our rating ranks him sixth of ten.

runners_data.name: Packetofbiscuits
runners_data.note: Holds a genuine late-running style in reality — though mapped to midfield here due to hold-up congestion — so John Mackie's charge is unlikely to secure its preferred rearward berth; carrying a blinker and returning after 110 days, its best AW form (2W from 15 runs on sim going) tends to come when able to drop in and produce a sustained run, which may be harder to execute than the map suggests.
runners_data.comment: Packetofbiscuits has shown ability at his best, winning twice in his last six starts, but a seventh and an unplaced run since and a 110-day absence make him hard to fancy, and he is ranked ninth of ten on our figures.

runners_data.name: He's A Gentleman
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's seven-year-old, fitted with a visor, is a true hold-up horse who has placed six times on similar Standard surfaces from 15 qualifying runs but finds himself operationally displaced by the field's shape; Oisin Murphy is an elite booking, and the horse's authentic late-running instincts — genuine, not redistributed — give him a live chance if a clear line of running opens approaching the final furlong.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked eighth of ten on our figures, He's A Gentleman faces a stiff task, with his trainer in poor recent form at 1/22 over the last 14 days; experience over today's trip and going at least offers some familiarity.

runners_data.name: Spaceman
runners_data.note: Richard & Peter Fahey's three-year-old has a smart sim-going profile (1W3P from 4 runs) and steps up in trip from recent shorter-distance efforts; a prominent type for Oisin Orr who will be caught up in the positional scramble, and the distance question at 7f is yet to be fully answered.
runners_data.comment: Spaceman showed he can win at this level when successful two starts back, and a third last time out keeps him in decent nick, but he has not always dominated from this draw and 126 lb is no featherweight ask for a 76-rated colt returning after 22 days.

runners_data.name: Shaw Park
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner for Scott Dixon, returning after 160 days off at OR 68 — the lightest weight in the field; Mikkel Mortensen (5lb claimer) rides and while Shaw Park should dictate uncontested, the lengthy absence and modest sim-going record (1W from 10 runs) raises doubts about whether he can sustain his early advantage through the final two furlongs.
runners_data.comment: Shaw Park has been winless in his last five starts, with an eighth last time out and a third three starts back his most notable efforts, and 160 days off the track does little to inspire confidence; ranked last on our figures, he faces a stiff ask here.

races.paceDynamic: Shaw Park is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with only one horse likely to press from the front, should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop across the 7f Wolverhampton AW trip. Behind him, four runners — Inside Story, Percy's Lad, Haaderr and Spaceman — all want to race prominently, creating a meaningful scrap for position in the first two furlongs and likely producing traffic congestion around the 2-3 furlong marker as they jostle for the best slots. Packetofbiscuits and He's A Gentleman are genuine hold-up horses but the field's pace profile has displaced them into mapped midfield positions they won't naturally occupy, meaning the rear of the field is likely thinner than it appears on paper. With a single front-runner setting an honest but uncontested tempo and a cluttered prominent group behind, this race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with a reliable late kick — those who can settle quietly away from the prominent scrimmage and time their run through the closing stages will be at a structural advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Shaw Park Controls, Closers Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Shaw Park dictates a steady-to-honest solo pace and the prominent group's energy is consumed fighting each other for position.
scenarios.body: Shaw Park sets a manageable tempo through the early stages, leaving the prominent quartet to waste energy scrambling for berths, which softens them approaching the final two furlongs; runners with a genuine late gear who have settled cleanly behind the mayhem are then best placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage, Strong Stayer Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the battle for prominent positions forces a faster early tempo that tests stamina and filters out the less genuine stayers.
scenarios.body: The four prominent types push against each other early, lifting the pace above Shaw Park's comfort zone and turning this into a more genuinely run contest; horses with proven 7f stamina on this surface who can race just off the pace without burning fuel in the opening scramble then come through late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Shaw Park Soft-Pedals, Front Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Shaw Park gets a completely uncontested lead at a crawl and the prominent group sit passively, handing him a winning tempo.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing to apply pressure, Shaw Park slows the pace to a dawdle and the prominent horses behind him also dawdle rather than challenge; the race becomes a sprint from 2f out and the horse who has controlled position and energy from the front has every chance of holding on.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Unfolds, Outsider Profits
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion causes significant interference or checks at a critical stage, mixing the field and unsettling favoured runners.
scenarios.body: Traffic trouble between the 3f and 2f marks disrupts the expected finishing order, with horses knocked sideways or forced wide, gifting a clean run to an unconsidered runner sitting in a fortuitous position.

watchPoints.text: Percy's Lad, Inside Story, Haaderr and Spaceman all want prominent positions — watch the first two furlongs for hard bumping or crowding as four runners compete for three realistic berths directly behind Shaw Park.

Shaw Park's 160-day absence is the single biggest pace-shape risk — if he is short of his peak fitness, he may capitulate from the front sooner than expected, turning this from a controlled-tempo race into a more chaotic finish that scrambles the tactical logic entirely.

He's A Gentleman and Packetofbiscuits are genuine hold-up horses operating out of their natural role — watch whether Murphy on He's A Gentleman attempts to drop him back further than the map suggests, creating a gap between the midfield cluster and the rear that could leave him isolated with no cover.

Naepoint's 332-day absence warrants monitoring in the pre-race paddock and early in the race — a fit-looking horse who jumps and travels smoothly would upgrade its chance significantly, while any sign of greenness or sluggishness would confirm the layoff as prohibitive.

races.name: Surestore Self Storage Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Khepri
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner here with headgear (visor) fitted, trained by K.R. Burke who is in strong form at 7/30 over 14 days; three starts have all produced fourth-place efforts but this is a far simpler pace scenario than her turf outings at Goodwood, and the uncontested lead at Wolverhampton over 1m½f on Standard is a significant upgrade in race conditions.
runners_data.comment: Khepri has been fourth in each of her last three starts and, rated 10 lb below her official mark on our figures, she looks up against it here, making her hard to fancy despite a reasonable break of 21 days since she last appeared.

runners_data.name: Blue Celestial
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa takes the ride for James Tate, and this filly has finished placed in nine of twelve starts on Standard AW going including two recent runner-up efforts at this trip and track combination; a natural hold-up operator who will settle mid-to-rear and needs the pace to be genuine enough to allow her staying profile to assert late.
runners_data.comment: Blue Celestial has been knocking persistently on the door, finishing second twice in her last three starts, and her experience over today's trip and going gives her every chance from stall one carrying 134 lb; the sole concern is that she remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Albertini Star
runners_data.note: Luke Morris partners this Alan King-trained three-year-old who has placed in two of five Standard-going starts including a second at Goodwood, but her AW sim-going record reads 0W0P from five attempts at this surface and the step back up in distance after a run over 8f is a query.
runners_data.comment: Albertini Star has been running into a place in her last two starts — third and second — and has run over today's trip and going before, with 26 days between runs suggesting she arrives fresh; winless in her last five, though, and ranked seventh of ten on our figures, she faces a stiff ask from stall eight carrying 133 lb.

runners_data.name: Samra Star
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy is a notable jockey booking for Linda Perratt's consistent five-year-old who has won twice and placed multiple times this season, including two wins on Good and a placed effort at Wolverhampton on Standard; headgear (hood) fitted and carrying 139lbs, she is a genuine closer whose form makes her among the most credible challengers if she can get a run from the back.
runners_data.comment: Samra Star arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and brings experience of today's trip and conditions, but her official mark of 62 and 139 lb burden may blunt that momentum, and an eighth two starts further back serves as a reminder she is not entirely consistent.

runners_data.name: Gladiadora
runners_data.note: The only prominent-style runner likely to sit directly behind Khepri, trained by Charlie Clover who has sent out two winners from eight runners in the past 14 days; her Standard AW form shows 2W4P from seven starts at 7-8f but she steps up in trip to 1m½f here, which is worth monitoring as a potential stamina query.
runners_data.comment: Gladiadora arrives here in sound nick after 29 days off, and her second two starts back shows she can hit the frame; yet to win in recent starts, though her experience over today's trip and going, combined with a rating of 68 that just edges her to the top of these, makes her the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Goldie Trickett
runners_data.note: David Egan rides for Jane Chapple-Hyam, and this four-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse by nature whose best recent effort was a third at Nottingham; she has been repositioned to midfield on the pace map because of the volume of true closers in this field, meaning she may race further forward than is ideal and her STYLE_FIT score of 0.91 tempers expectations accordingly.
runners_data.comment: Goldie Trickett has run over today's trip and going before, and her rating of 67 marks her out as a strong threat at the head of these rankings, with a third in recent starts suggesting consistent ability; the main risk is she remains winless in her last five.

runners_data.name: Mimi's Magic
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop's three-year-old has a visor in the headgear notes and placed in three of eight starts including a runner-up effort at Wolverhampton on Standard going; genuinely a hold-up type by style but with so many closers in this field she is mapped to midfield — a real closer forced to race in an unnatural slot, which marginally dims her chance of producing her best.
runners_data.comment: Mimi's Magic has shown steady progression deep in her recent form, finishing second and third in her last five starts, and she has run over today's trip and going before; the concern is that she has drifted back to sixth and eighth since, leaving her yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Sailor's Return
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope partners this David O'Meara runner who has headgear (tongue-tie) fitted and whose last seven runs include no wins or places on this surface configuration; by nature a hold-up horse shuffled to midfield given the glut of closers, and her STYLE_FIT of 0.90 — the lowest in the field — combined with a flat recent form string of 446604 makes her hard to trust.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked eighth of ten on our figures, Sailor's Return faces a stiff ask, though she has run over today's trip before and returns on a quick turnaround of just 15 days.

runners_data.name: Sunshine And Roses
runners_data.note: Jack Channon's trainer has sent this three-year-old out for a third time in 10 days with no winners from 10 runners in the past fortnight, which is a concern; she won on Standard AW last time out and is a genuine closer by style though mapped to midfield here, with her STYLE_FIT of 0.93 indicating she will be racing out of her natural position — Rose Dawes' 5lb claim helps on the weights.
runners_data.comment: Landed a win two starts back but had to settle for second last time out, and her record in recent starts is mixed; has run over today's trip and going, and at 130 lb from stall five she has plenty to prove if that consistent form is to resurface.

runners_data.name: Delevingne Dream
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace's lightly-raced three-year-old has headgear (pads) fitted and a form string of 0-077 suggesting she has struggled to get involved on the AW; a true hold-up type placed in midfield here due to the field's profile, and with a STYLE_FIT of 0.92 and no wins or places from four Standard-going starts, she looks the hardest to make a case for in this company.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, with a pair of seventh-place finishes her best recent efforts, Delevingne Dream cuts a difficult profile on these figures and ranks last of the ten runners; stall two and experience over today's trip offer slim comfort.

races.paceDynamic: Khepri is the sole confirmed front-runner in this ten-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she will set a controlled, uncontested tempo on Standard Wolverhampton ground over 1m½f. That lone-pace scenario creates a race run at a sustainable rhythm where the leader dictates every fraction, conserves energy through the middle stages, and can quicken away from her rivals in the straight without having burned fuel in a speed duel. The back half of the field is dominated by hold-up types — Mimi's Magic, Sailor's Return, Sunshine And Roses, Goldie Trickett and Delevingne Dream — all genuine closers who have been pushed into midfield on the map because there are simply too many hold-up horses for the race shape to accommodate naturally at the rear. Gladiadora is the only prominent runner likely to sit just off Khepri's shoulder and represent any form of pressure. This race shape strongly favours the leader or a close-tracking prominent type: a controlled, front-run tempo over an extended flat trip on an AW oval rewards those who travel in the first two or three positions and never have to mount a sustained late challenge from off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Khepri Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Khepri is allowed to bowl along at her own pace and Gladiadora can only track from second without applying any real pressure.
scenarios.body: Khepri dictates the fractions from the front, conserves enough energy through the bend, and simply finds more in the straight than her rivals can summon from further back; a lone front-runner on Standard Wolverhampton AW over this trip is notoriously hard to reel in without a strong gallop to play into closers' hands.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Gladiadora travels strongly just off the pace and Khepri fades late, allowing a close tracker to pounce in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Gladiadora or a horse that manages to race in the first three positions without using excessive energy absorbs the lead runner late and asserts in the straight; this shape rewards any horse with the tactical sense to sit second or third and pounce when Khepri's early advantage begins to ebb.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If Khepri sets a genuinely strong gallop that burns out the prominent horses and creates enough pace for a finisher to close ground in the straight.
scenarios.body: One of the better-credentialled hold-up types — Samra Star or Blue Celestial, both with solid form on Standard going — makes sustained late headway as the front has gone too hard; Samra Star's recent winning form on Good and her experience as a five-year-old give her the best profile to deliver a late challenge if the pace is honest enough.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart
scenarios.trigger: If Khepri misses the break or is checked early, stripping the race of its sole pace source and creating a messy, slowly-run contest with a falsely slow tempo.
scenarios.body: Without a genuine pace-setter the field bunches, the race is run in a compressed fashion and produces a sprint-finish from the home turn that favours whoever secures a clear run soonest; Sunshine And Roses, with a recent win on Standard AW ground, and Gladiadora, with prominent tendencies, are best equipped to benefit from positional chaos.

watchPoints.text: Khepri's ability to control tempo unchallenged is the fulcrum of this race — if she is slow away or settles slower than usual, the entire race shape collapses and Gladiadora becomes the de-facto pace-setter.

Samra Star carries top weight of 139lbs and Gladiadora also carries 139lbs — monitor both in the early stages to see whether the burden affects their position in the first half-mile, particularly on a 1m½f trip that demands sustained effort.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up types — Mimi's Magic, Sailor's Return, Sunshine And Roses, Goldie Trickett and Delevingne Dream — will be fighting for real estate in a congested midfield; watch for traffic problems entering the straight as five horses attempt to find gaps simultaneously.

Blue Celestial's jockey booking of Silvestre De Sousa is an upgrade from recent rides and her record of 0W7P on similar going suggests she hits the frame regularly without winning — a market move would be worth noting if punters identify an angle the raw stats obscure.

Sunshine And Roses won last time on this surface and carries a 5lb claimer in Rose Dawes, which offsets her weight, but Jack Channon's 14-day strike rate of 0/10 is a cold trainer angle that should temper enthusiasm for any market support.

races.name: Maggies Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Up The Agenda
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse whose best form at this course and trip on Standard going (win) is a key asset, but Callum Shepherd must manoeuvre from the rear on a track where 6f gives limited time to reel in a controlled pace-setter; 34 days off is acceptable.
runners_data.comment: Up The Agenda won four starts back and was third five starts back, but three successive out-of-the-money efforts since, the latest 34 days ago, leave him needing to rediscover that form; experience over today's trip and going helps, though 135 lb from stall 1 is the balancing act.

runners_data.name: Percy's Star
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner wearing a hood, De Sousa in the saddle is a major positive for a horse that can dictate on its own terms; steps up to 6f from 5f, which is not guaranteed to suit a speedball type, but course form is absent so distance stamina is an open question.
runners_data.comment: Percy's Star showed he can win at this level when landing a success two starts back, and he has experience over today's trip to call on. Carrying 135 lb from stall four, the 45-day break is worth monitoring, though his overall profile makes him the one to follow here.

runners_data.name: Acclaimed Freedom
runners_data.note: Murphy's booking lifts the profile considerably; hold-up style needs a stronger pace than Percy's Star is likely to generate, and the pair of 7f Wolverhampton starts on Standard (finishing 6th and 8th) are a flag, though the 6f drop in trip is more aligned with the horse's best efforts on Good ground.
runners_data.comment: Acclaimed Freedom shaped with promise when second three starts back, and with experience over today's trip and going, he arrives from stall two carrying 134 lb as a leading danger here; the risk is that he has been winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Sargent Dennis
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with three runs at this course on Standard going, recording a win and two placed efforts — an ideal tactical profile for today's likely race shape; Rose Dawes's 5lb claim is helpful but the trainer's 0/10 in the 14-day window mildly tempers confidence.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Sargent Dennis faces a stiff ask, though he has run over today's trip and going before and arrives here on the back of a win two starts back, with a second three starts back adding further encouragement to that sequence.

runners_data.name: Arishka's Dream
runners_data.note: Has won, placed twice and shown course-and-distance form on Standard going across seven visits, making the profile highly relevant; trainer Kubler in strong 14-day form (5/16) adds confidence, though 75 days off is the longest absence in this field and merits monitoring in the market.
runners_data.comment: Arishka's Dream showed smart form when winning and finishing second twice in a productive spell, and his rating of 79 has him joint-top of this field on an 8-runner card, with experience of both today's trip and going a solid foundation; the chief concern is two successive eighths since that purple patch.

runners_data.name: Escape Plan
runners_data.note: Won on Standard at this course and distance, but the horse's natural instinct is to race off the pace — mapped to midfield here because the hold-up slots are full, meaning Sean Levey may find the horse trading closer than ideal; the tongue-tie is noted and the 14-day return flags yard activity.
runners_data.comment: Escape Plan has finished seventh or eighth in three of his last four starts, making him hard to fancy on recent evidence, though he did win four starts back and has experience of both today's trip and going conditions.

runners_data.name: Fizzy Cristal
runners_data.note: An off-the-pace horse by preference whose last win came on Standard going at this track, but Warren Fentiman (3) inherits a runner that is likely squeezed towards a midfield position that does not suit its finishing pattern; the Fahey yard is active (5/29) which keeps the horse relevant despite the style constraint.
runners_data.comment: Fizzy Cristal showed she can win in recent starts, scoring a first four runs back, though she has finished fifth in each of her last two outings and faces a stiff task from stall eight carrying 128 lb.

runners_data.name: Soca Star
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose course form on Standard over 6f produced only one placed effort from eleven starts at this track-going combination — a thin return that makes this profile harder to back; 50 days absent and a jockey booking without notable course stats adds to the caution.
runners_data.comment: Soca Star has shown genuine ability in recent starts, finishing second and third in her last five, and she has experience over today's trip and conditions; drawn in stall three carrying 128 lb, the main concern is that she has been winless in recent starts and has not run for 50 days.

races.paceDynamic: Percy's Star is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to press from the gates, Silvestre De Sousa should control this 6f Wolverhampton contest from the outset, setting a sustainable rather than frantic pace. Sargent Dennis and Arishka's Dream will push to sit prominently just off the leader, creating a compact early order but without the aggressive pace injection that would destabilise Percy's Star's rhythm. The hold-up contingent — Up The Agenda and Acclaimed Freedom — must make their ground from further back on a track where the straight is short and Wolverhampton's configuration can make late momentum difficult to sustain over 6f on a Standard surface. This field holds more hold-up horses than the map can naturally accommodate at the rear: Escape Plan and Fizzy Cristal are genuine off-the-pace types who have been mapped to midfield but may struggle to find their natural position if the prominent horses dictate a steady early tempo that compresses the field. The race shape strongly favours prominent racers tracking a controlled pace — horses with the tactical speed to sit second or third and produce a decisive move turning for home.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Percy's Star Controls Freely
scenarios.trigger: If Percy's Star leads unopposed and sets a measured, sustainable gallop that suits those racing just behind.
scenarios.body: De Sousa dictates on Percy's Star, and the prominent stalkers Sargent Dennis and Arishka's Dream sit ideally placed to pounce approaching the final furlong with minimal ground to make up. This controlled shape is the dominant race outcome given the lack of any pressure on the leader, rewarding horses with positional efficiency over raw closing ability.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Percy's Star ties up late and one of the prominent chasers produces superior late speed to drive past.
scenarios.body: Sargent Dennis and Arishka's Dream both carry strong form at this course and distance on Standard going, and either is capable of wearing down a front-runner who has used energy controlling the race. This shape still rewards positional horses and does not require any hold-up runner to produce an extraordinary late burst.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to compress the field and leave a late gap for a closer to arrive.
scenarios.body: Up The Agenda or Acclaimed Freedom would need Percy's Star to go off too quickly for a stakes-quality sprint, which the pace dynamic does not suggest is likely on this card. Oisin Murphy on Acclaimed Freedom is the jockey best equipped to exploit any such collapse, and Up The Agenda's win at this course and distance on Standard offers a live each-way platform if the shape opens up.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Outrun
scenarios.trigger: If Escape Plan or Fizzy Cristal secure an unexpectedly prominent early position and benefit from racing closer than their natural style.
scenarios.body: Both are tagged as true hold-up horses whose redistribution to midfield reflects positional reality rather than preference, making this scenario contingent on an atypical run style that discounts their expected finishing effort. The low probability reflects that the race shape must deviate significantly from the expected tempo for either to win from an unnatural position.

watchPoints.text: Percy's Star's stamina for 6f is unproven — if the horse ties up in the final furlong having controlled the race, Sargent Dennis and Arishka's Dream are ideally placed to punish it.
Arishka's Dream is 75 days off and, despite strong course form, a flat or drifting early market move would suggest the yard is not fully confident after the layoff.

Escape Plan and Fizzy Cristal are natural hold-up horses compressed into midfield — watch whether either attempts to race forward from the gate, which would be a significant change of tactics and could reshape the pace entirely.

Oisin Murphy's booking for Acclaimed Freedom is the highest-profile jockey appointment in the race — if the market shortens the horse meaningfully pre-race, it signals Murphy expects a stronger pace than the map suggests.

Sargent Dennis has placed on his last two Standard runs at Wolverhampton over 6f; a prominent position behind Percy's Star is almost guaranteed given style, making early sectionals the key to whether the front-runner can be reeled in.

races.name: Self Storage Association Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Dance Time
runners_data.note: Consistent stayer for Loughnane who wants a prominent pitch but has mixed form at this trip, finishing 7th at Goodwood over 16f last time; only 7 days since last run is worth noting, and similar-going record of 8 runs with 3 places from 4 positions suggests she stays the trip but needs a strong pace to land a blow.
runners_data.comment: Dance Time arrives here just seven days after finishing second last time out, and with experience of today's trip and conditions, she shapes as a live threat carrying 140 lb — the main risk is that she remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Percy Jones
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old veteran for Mark Loughnane who races prominently but has been out 36 days and has shown a recent pattern of struggling at 12f on good, making this step back to 14f on Standard more interesting; placed form at 14f on Standard exists but overall profile suggests he finds one or two too good at this level.

runners_data.name: White Storm
runners_data.note: Three-year-old Crisford runner ridden by De Sousa who leads from the front and has competitive form — a runner-up at 11f on Standard is encouraging — but this is a significant step up to 1m6f for a young horse who has run only three times; how the stamina holds when challenged by Velvet Whisper is the central question.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, White Storm faces a stiff ask off 134 lb, though a second three starts back offers a crumb of encouragement and a trainer firing at 36% over the past fortnight keeps connections hopeful.

runners_data.name: So Alex
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with two second-place finishes at 14f on good, including a recent runner-up, making this step to 16f and the track switch the key questions; trainer T14 record of 0/3 gives no confidence from a stable angle, but the horse carries his form into the race on merit and the trip extension could unlock more stamina.
runners_data.comment: Placed second in two of his last four starts but only fifth last time out, So Alex arrives 46 days between runs and carrying 142 lb; he has run over today's trip and going, and a rating of 78 offers a sliver of encouragement, though recent consistency remains mixed.

runners_data.name: Velvet Whisper
runners_data.note: Tudhope takes over on this Bethell mare who has two wins on her CV including at 12f on soft and 10f, but has been beaten an aggregate of well over 30 lengths in two runs on good; 102 days off is a major flag, and her front-running style demands peak fitness — she may find White Storm too persistent and this layoff a vulnerability.
runners_data.comment: Velvet Whisper showed real ability when winning back-to-back three and four starts back, and a trainer firing at 41% makes her impossible to ignore off a mark of 74; the concern is two successive eighths since, plus 102 days off the track.

runners_data.name: Kingdom Of Stars
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Kerry Lee who was 8th at this track last time over 16f on Standard, so course form is not encouraging on a bare reading; however, the strong pace scenario this race will produce is exactly the shape that suits a stayer dropping in from 20f races on good ground, and Havlin is an astute jockey for these situations.
runners_data.comment: Kingdom Of Stars shaped with real promise when second three starts back and third four starts back, and our ratings just edge him top of these on paper; the worry is that winless in his last five, his latest eighth needs explaining.

runners_data.name: Heroics
runners_data.note: Three-year-old for Alan King with Oisin Murphy aboard, a partnership that commands respect; sits prominently and won over 14f on good, but 1m6f is uncharted territory and his one run on Standard (second at 11f) gives limited surface evidence — Murphy's positioning skill will be crucial in the traffic-heavy midfield.
runners_data.comment: Beaten fifth last time out, Heroics heads into this ranked seventh of nine on our figures, making him hard to fancy despite a win two starts back and experience of both today's trip and going conditions.

runners_data.name: Flash Kozo
runners_data.note: Winner at 14f on Standard at Wolverhampton on most recent run which is a directly relevant data point for this race; holds up at the back and is 22 days fresh, which is adequate, and trainer Eustace has one win from nine in the 14-day window — the Wolverhampton course knowledge and staying profile make him well-placed for the expected pace collapse scenario.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out off a mark of 70, giving Flash Kozo an obvious fitness edge at 22 days, and he has run over today's trip and going before; however, he carries 129 lb and his speed rating of 66 leaves him ranked sixth of nine, suggesting he faces a stiff ask against stronger rivals.

runners_data.name: Kakirra
runners_data.note: In sparkling form with four wins from his last five starts, this Sangster three-year-old is naturally a prominent racer by inclination but finds himself mapped to midfield because the race holds too many forward-going types to accommodate him — racing out of his preferred role at a 16f trip he is yet to test means a discount is warranted despite his excellent recent figures.
runners_data.comment: Ranked eighth of nine on our figures, Kakirra is hard to fancy at the weights despite a lively recent run of form that includes four wins in his last six starts, most recently a runner-up finish, and he has experience of today's distance and going.

races.paceDynamic: White Storm and Velvet Whisper are confirmed front-runners who will clash immediately for the lead over 1m6f at Wolverhampton, creating a genuinely contested early pace that is unlikely to relent at this trip. Dance Time, Percy Jones, So Alex, and Heroics all want prominent positions behind them, generating a congested group through the first half mile that raises significant traffic danger approaching the 2-3 furlong marker. Kakirra is a genuine prominent type pushed into a midfield map position simply because the race has more forward-going horses than the shape can accommodate — of the true front-runners, White Storm with De Sousa aboard for Crisford's powerful operation is most likely to actually control the rail, with Velvet Whisper applying pressure rather than leading comfortably. This contested pace over a staying trip on a fair surface favours hold-up horses and late-finishing mid-division types who can track the carnage and benefit from a strong, honest gallop — Kingdom Of Stars and Flash Kozo are best placed structurally to exploit this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If White Storm and Velvet Whisper battle throughout and ensure the pace is genuinely hot from the outset.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners drain each other's stamina, leaving the prominent cluster vulnerable in the straight and giving hold-up horses a true run to aim at; over 1m6f on Standard ground this is the textbook outcome when two genuine leaders meet.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Player Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If one front-runner cedes early and the pace settles just enough for a prominent racer to travel comfortably and produce a well-timed challenge.
scenarios.body: A horse like So Alex or Heroics, sitting just behind a controlled tempo, can produce their effort without being swamped by the early duel; this suits runners with proven placed form at this trip who have enough class to quicken off a decent but not ruinous gallop.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Velvet Whisper or White Storm breaks cleanly and the other fails to match strides, allowing one to control the race on their own terms.
scenarios.body: A solo leader over 1m6f can set an economical enough gallop to maintain their advantage into the straight, and Velvet Whisper's two wins over similar distances show she is capable when unopposed; De Sousa on White Storm is equally equipped to dictate if Velvet Whisper is slow to stride.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Very Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is extreme and the entire prominent group fades badly entering the straight, leaving the two genuine hold-up types with a clear run.
scenarios.body: Kingdom Of Stars would need to find a clean passage from the rear after struggling at this track last time, while Flash Kozo's recent Wolverhampton win over 14f shows he can finish powerfully on this surface; this scenario requires a perfect storm of collapse up front and clear sailing from behind.

watchPoints.text: White Storm and Velvet Whisper are both genuine front-runners — watch the first furlong closely for a genuine battle that could set a pace damaging to both their chances and the entire prominent cluster.

Prominent congestion with Dance Time, Percy Jones, So Alex, Heroics and the displaced Kakirra all wanting to sit in the first four means serious traffic danger between the 2f and 3f poles — any horse caught wide or squeezed could lose its race here.
Velvet Whisper has not run for 102 days — watch the market for any drifting in the betting that signals trainer concern about fitness, as her front-running style demands she be at peak condition.

Kakirra's outstanding recent form (four wins from five) will attract support but its position in this race shape is structurally compromised — watch whether Crouch elects to push forward from the off or accepts the midfield slot.

Flash Kozo's course-and-distance win at Wolverhampton over 14f on Standard is the most directly applicable recent piece of form in the race — monitor how confidently Fraser settles him at the rear, as any traffic trouble on the turn will compromise his finishing run.
